item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 092317
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Fri Oct 9 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles west of the southern tip
of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane Simon, located a
couple of hundred miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala early next week. Environmental conditions are expected to
be conducive for gradual development thereafter, and a tropical
depression is likely to form by the latter half of next week as the
system moves generally west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 51a
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 092345
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Intermediate Advisory Number 51A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
500 PM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026
 
...RACHEL STARTING TO ACCELERATE TOWARD BAJA CALIFORNIA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM PDT...0000 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...23.6N 123.7W
ABOUT 875 MI...1410 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 745 MI...1200 KM SW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 50 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...995 MB...29.39 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California, from San Jose de Las Palomas
northward to the U.S./Mexico Border
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Southern California coast from the U.S/Mexico Border northward to
the San Diego/Orange County Line
* East coast of Baja California, from Isla San Luis northward to
Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests in northern Baja California, northern Gulf of California,
and Southern California should continue to monitor the progress of
Rachel.
 
For storm information specific to your area in the United
States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
forecast office. For storm information specific to your area
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by
your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM PDT (0000 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 23.6 North, longitude 123.7 West. Rachel is
moving toward the northeast near 9 mph (15 km/h). A general 
northeast to north-northeast motion, with a significant increase in 
forward speed, is expected over the next couple of days. On the 
forecast track, the center of Rachel is expected to approach the 
northern Baja California Peninsula or Southern California late 
Saturday or early Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Some strengthening is possible the next day or so, but rapid 
weakening forecast after the storm moves inland over the 
southwestern United States on Sunday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 995 mb (29.39 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected to reach portions of 
western Baja California within the Tropical Storm Warning area 
starting Saturday evening or night. Tropical storm conditions are 
also possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area in extreme 
Southern California and eastern Baja California beginning late 
Saturday night or early Sunday. Strong gusty winds associated with 
the system are expected to spread over interior portions of the 
Southwest United States, especially in areas of higher terrain, from 
this weekend into early next week.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of
Baja California this weekend.
 
Rachel and associated moisture of the system will also bring
rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5
inches in portions of the Southwest United States this weekend. This
will lead to increasing coverage of rainfall and potential for flash
and urban flooding.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall 
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and 
the Flash Flood Risk graphic at 
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast 
of Southern California and northern Baja California through the 
weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions, as well as moderate to isolated major 
coastal flooding, through early next week.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 51
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 092044
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  51
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026
 
Rachel is producing limited convection this afternoon, with 
relatively shallow, warm cloud tops confined to the northern and 
eastern semicircles. A scatterometer pass at 1753 UTC showed peak 
satellite-derived winds of 37 kt. Satellite intensity estimates from 
UW-CIMSS and TAFB range between 26 and 41 kt. Using this data, the 
initial intensity is lowered to 40 kt for this advisory.
 
The system is starting to gradually increase its forward speed and 
is moving at an estimated 055/5 kt. Rachel should begin to 
accelerate toward the northeast and then north-northeast tonight and 
tomorrow, embedded within the flow of a deepening mid- to 
upper-level trough approaching the western United States. On the 
forecast track, the system is expected to move inland over northern 
Baja California late Saturday or early Sunday before continuing 
north-northeastward into the southwestern United States on Sunday. 
Track guidance remains similar to the previous cycle, with the 
hurricane regional models, the GFS, and the ECMWF on the left side 
of the envelope, and the GDMI and HCCA on the right. The NHC track 
forecast is essentially an update of the previous one and lies in 
the middle of the guidance envelope. Note that there will be a sharp 
gradient in the wind field, with the strongest winds anticipated to 
remain primarily in the eastern and southern semicircles of the 
circulation.
 
Rachel continues to struggle to produce anything more than shallow 
convection, as the system is embedded within a dry and stable air 
mass over cool sea surface temperatures. However, as the system 
begins to accelerate northeastward, a favorable trough interaction 
is expected, along with an increase in mid-level relative humidity. 
Also, sea surface temperatures just offshore of the western Baja 
California peninsula are anomalously warm for this time of year. 
Given these conditions, Rachel is expected to produce intermittent 
bursts of convection and strengthen, up until landfall, even though 
vertical wind shear will increase significantly as the system 
approaches the coast. Once inland, rapid weakening is expected, and 
the system is forecast to become post-tropical over the southwestern 
United States. The latest NHC intensity forecast is similar to the 
previous advisory and lies near the upper end of the guidance 
envelope, although some of the hurricane regional models and the 
HCCA are slightly higher than the official forecast just offshore at 
36 h.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to approach the coast of the northern Baja 
California Peninsula and extreme Southern California at tropical 
storm strength Saturday night.  Tropical storm conditions are 
expected over portions of western Baja California, Mexico where 
Tropical Storm Warnings are in effect. Tropical storm conditions are 
possible in extreme Southern California and eastern Baja California 
where a Tropical Storm Watch is in effect.
 
2. Damaging wind gusts associated with Rachel and its remnants are
expected to spread over portions of northwestern Mexico and interior
portions of the Southwest United States, especially in areas of
higher terrain, Saturday night and Sunday.
 
3. Rachel and its moisture will spread over portions of the
Southwest United States and northern Baja California peninsula
through this weekend. This will lead to increasing coverage of
rainfall and for the potential for significant flash and urban
flooding.
 
4. Swells partly generated by Rachel will continue to build along
the coast of Southern California and northern Baja California.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions, as well as moderate to isolated major coastal
flooding, through early next week.  Please consult products from
your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  09/2100Z 23.3N 124.0W   40 KT  45 MPH
 12H  10/0600Z 24.2N 122.4W   45 KT  50 MPH
 24H  10/1800Z 26.7N 119.4W   50 KT  60 MPH
 36H  11/0600Z 30.9N 117.2W   55 KT  65 MPH
 48H  11/1800Z 36.4N 115.0W   40 KT  45 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 60H  12/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 092045
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 PM CST Fri Oct 09 2026
 
...SIMON CONTINUES TO STRENGTHEN...
...PREPARATIONS TO PROTECT LIFE AND PROPERTY SHOULD BE RUSHED TO
COMPLETION TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.2N 104.7W
ABOUT 195 MI...315 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 295 MI...480 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...105 MPH...165 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...966 MB...28.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has issued a Hurricane Watch for the
coast of mainland Mexico from San Blas to El Roblito and for Las
Islas Marias.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Punta Mita to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Additional watches or warnings could be required for portions of the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located 
near latitude 16.2 North, longitude 104.7 West. Simon is moving 
toward the northwest near 2 mph (4 km/h). A gradual turn toward the 
north with a slight increase in forward speed is expected through 
tonight. Simon is then forecast to move generally northward, with 
the center passing very near or over the west-central coast of 
Mexico late Saturday or Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 105 mph (165 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Additional rapid strengthening is expected 
during the next day or so. Simon is forecast to become a major 
hurricane this evening and strengthen further on Saturday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles
(130 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 966 mb (28.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND:  Hurricane conditions are expected in the Hurricane Warning 
area Saturday evening or Sunday, with tropical storm conditions 
expected as soon as Saturday morning. Hurricane conditions are 
possible in the Hurricane Watch area beginning Sunday afternoon, 
with tropical storm conditions possible as soon as Sunday morning.  
Tropical storm conditions are possible within the Tropical Storm 
Watch area beginning tonight or early Saturday.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 10 to 20 
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum 
totals of 30 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, Colima, 
Jalisco and Nayarit through Sunday.  This rainfall will produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE:  A dangerous storm surge is likely along the
immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes
landfall. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 600 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 092046
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 PM CST Fri Oct 09 2026
 
An intermittent warm spot in the CDO of Simon has been present since 
this morning, co-located with a small pinhole-like eye noted in 
visible imagery. The initial intensity of 90 kt is based primarily 
on the latest TAFB Dvorak fix, though this is very uncertain due to 
the very small size of Simon and intensity estimates range from 
around 65 kt (DMINT) to 97 KT (RCM-1 SAR). The SAR data this morning 
indicated the system has an RMW near 5 n mi, highlighting how small 
it is.

Simon has continued to strengthen today, although at a slightly 
slower rate since this morning. Further rapid intensification is 
still anticipated but the exact timing of when the rate might pick 
up again is highly uncertain. Small hurricanes like Simon are 
particularly susceptible to large and rapid fluctuations in 
intensity. In the short term, no changes of note were made to the 
NHC intensity forecast, which remains at the high end of the 
guidance envelope. 

The main challenge with this forecast is how sensitive it is to the 
exact track Simon takes over the next 2 days and whether or not it 
moves inland over the Mexican states of Colima and Jalisco. A track 
slightly east of the NHC official forecast track will cause Simon to 
quickly dissipate and minimize the threat of wind impacts farther 
north in Mexico. However, a track just to the west would likely 
allow Simon to move much farther north as a hurricane. At this time, 
the difference between these track scenarios is less than the 
average error of NHC forecasts. Most of the deterministic global 
models shifted slightly east this cycle, but ensemble guidance 
indicates both scenarios are still plausible. The NHC track and 
intensity forecast therefore is largely unchanged and continues to 
show Simon tracking farther north than it might realistically make 
it to emphasize that risk. 
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a
Hurricane warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita.
Preparations to protect life and property should be completed by
late today.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall will produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.
 
3. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico through the weekend. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
